q.s: Lothal, the Harappan dockyard town near the Gulf of Khambhat, lies on which river?
q.x: Lothal lies on the Bhogava, near its confluence with the Sabarmati, not on the Narmada.

q.s: Daimabad, the southernmost Harappan site in Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra, lies on the bank of:
q.x: Daimabad lies on the Pravara, a tributary of the Godavari.

q.s: Which Harappan city was divided into three parts – citadel, middle town and lower town?
q.x: Dholavira in Kutch had a unique three-part plan; most Harappan towns had only a citadel and a lower town.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites had NO citadel?
q.x: Chanhudaro in Sindh had no citadel; Kalibangan, Harappa and Mohenjodaro had citadels.

q.s: The 'Dancing Girl' figurine found at Mohenjodaro is made of:
q.x: It is a bronze figure about 10.5 cm tall, cast by the lost-wax process; it is kept in the National Museum, New Delhi.

q.s: In June 2026, which body decided to restore the original image of the 'Dancing Girl' in the new Class 9 Art textbook?
q.x: It was the NCERT, the textbook body, not the CBSE.

q.s: Alamgirpur, a Late Harappan site and the easternmost Harappan settlement, is in present-day:
q.x: Alamgirpur lies in Meerut district of Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: The Mansehra inscription in present-day Pakistan is:
q.x: Mansehra, like Shahbazgarhi, has a set of Ashoka's major rock edicts; the Junagarh inscription belongs to Rudradaman.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, the term 'vrihi' denoted:
q.x: Vrihi was rice, which had ritual use; barley was yava and wheat godhuma.

q.s: Which of the following Later Vedic terms is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Yava was barley; wheat was godhuma, rice vrihi and iron krishna ayas.

q.s: The Mahabharata is divided into how many parvas (books)?
q.x: The Mahabharata has 18 parvas; its original core, the Jaya, had 8,800 shlokas.

q.s: Which work is appended to the Mahabharata as its supplement?
q.x: The Harivamsa, on the life of Krishna, is the appendix (khila) of the Mahabharata.

q.s: The entire Ninth Mandala of the Rigveda is devoted to hymns addressed to:
q.x: All hymns of the Ninth Mandala are addressed to Soma, the god of the sacred plant and drink.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Soma is correct?
o: Soma was a female deity of the dawn
Soma was a male deity of the sacred plant and drink
The Tenth Mandala is entirely devoted to Soma
Soma was the god of fire
q.x: Soma was male; Usha was the dawn goddess, Agni the fire god, and the Ninth Mandala is Soma's.

q.s: Which teacher of the Buddha's time preached Niyativada (fatalism) and led the Ajivikas?
q.x: Makkhali Gosala taught Niyativada; Akriyavada was the doctrine of Purana Kassapa.

q.s: 'Nigantha Nataputta', one of the six heterodox teachers in Buddhist texts, refers to:
q.x: Buddhist texts such as the Samannaphala Sutta call Mahavira Nigantha Nataputta.

q.s: The cognizance (symbol) of Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, is the:
q.x: Mahavira's symbol is the lion; the bull is Rishabhadeva's, the serpent Parshvanatha's and the conch Neminatha's.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Tirthankara – symbol) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Mahavira's symbol is the lion; the conch belongs to Neminatha.

q.s: In Jainism, a fully liberated soul is called a:
q.x: A liberated soul is a Siddha; Ganadharas are the chief disciples of a Tirthankara and Shravakas are lay followers.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Jainism is correct?
o: It rejects the authority of the Vedas
A fully liberated soul is called a Ganadhara
Householders can attain salvation without monastic life
q.x: Jainism rejects the Vedas; a liberated soul is a Siddha, salvation needs monastic life, and ajiva is non-conscious matter.

q.s: Who led the Jain monks, along with Chandragupta Maurya, to Shravanabelagola during a 12-year famine in Magadha?
q.x: Bhadrabahu led the migration south; Sthulabhadra stayed back in Magadha.

q.s: Chandragupta Maurya is said to have ended his life by sallekhana at:
q.x: Jain tradition holds that he died by fasting (sallekhana) at Chandragiri hill, Shravanabelagola.

q.s: The Hathigumpha inscription belongs to which ruler?
q.x: The Hathigumpha inscription near Bhubaneswar records the deeds of Kharavela of Kalinga, of the Mahameghavahana family.

q.s: In the Hathigumpha inscription, the river 'Kannabenna' refers to the:
q.x: Kannabenna is the Krishna; Kharavela sent his army westward up to it, ignoring Satakarni.

q.s: The 'urban decay' thesis for the post-Gupta period is associated with which historian?
q.x: R.S. Sharma pointed to shrinking towns and scarce gold coins; Pataliputra had declined by Hiuen-Tsang's visit.

q.s: Kiratarjuniyam, describing the combat between Arjuna and Shiva in the guise of a hunter, was written by:
q.x: Bharavi wrote Kiratarjuniyam; Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita is on Nala and Damayanti, and Dandin wrote Dashakumaracharita.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (work – author) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Naishadhiyacharita, on Nala and Damayanti, is by Sriharsha.

q.s: Shashanka of Gauda, the rival of Harshavardhana, had his capital at:
q.x: Shashanka ruled from Karnasuvarna in Bengal; Valabhi was the Maitraka capital.

q.s: Which king is said to have cut down the Bodhi tree at Gaya?
q.x: Hiuen-Tsang accuses Shashanka of cutting down the Bodhi tree; Devagupta of Malwa was his ally.

q.s: Under the Cholas, the 'Velaikkarar' were:
o: Bodyguards sworn to die with the king
q.x: Velaikkarar were the king's sworn bodyguards; Kaikkolar were infantry regiments and Kadagams cantonments.

q.s: 'Kadaram', taken by Rajendra Chola's naval expedition of 1025, is identified with:
q.x: Kadaram is Kedah in the Malay peninsula, part of the Srivijaya realm.

q.s: In Chola land terminology, the 'ulukudi' were:
q.x: Ulukudi were tenants; kaniyudaiyar were the land-owning farmers and karanmai the right to cultivate.

q.s: Which of the following Chola land terms is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Kaniyudaiyar were the land-owning farmers; the ulukudi were tenants.

q.s: Which Delhi Sultan was called 'Quran Khwan' because he recited the Quran melodiously?
q.x: Aibak earned the title Quran Khwan; he passed from the Qazi of Nishapur to Muhammad Ghori.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Qutbuddin Aibak is correct?
o: He died after a fall while playing chaugan at Lahore
He was bought by Mahmud of Ghazni
q.x: Aibak passed from the Qazi of Nishapur to Muhammad Ghori and died after a polo fall at Lahore in 1210.

q.s: Which Delhi Sultan kept the ulema out of state affairs, holding that the needs of the state came first?
q.x: Alauddin did not let the ulema guide policy; Firoz Tughlaq, by contrast, followed their counsel.

q.s: Under Sher Shah Suri, the term 'dagh' referred to:
q.x: Dagh was branding of horses and chehra the descriptive roll of soldiers; the silver coin was the rupiya.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Sher Shah Suri's administration?
o: Local headmen made responsible for tracing crime
q.x: The mansabdari system was Akbar's; the other three were Sher Shah's measures.

q.s: The French traveller Thevenot came to India during the reign of:
q.x: Thevenot reached Surat in 1666, in Aurangzeb's reign.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (European visitor – Mughal reign) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Thevenot came in 1666, in Aurangzeb's reign.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Ahmad Shah Abdali is NOT correct?
o: He had earlier been a general of Nadir Shah
In 1757 he placed Alamgir II on the Mughal throne
His raids into India began in 1748
Anand Ram Mukhlis was the contemporary historian of his Panipat campaign
q.x: Anand Ram Mukhlis chronicled Nadir Shah's invasion of 1739, not Abdali's Panipat campaign; the other three are correct.

q.s: 'Remonstrantie', an account of India under Jahangir, was written by the Dutch factor:
q.x: Pelsaert wrote Remonstrantie; Bernier was a French physician and Tavernier a French diamond merchant.

q.s: Pietra dura inlay was first used on a Mughal monument at the:
q.x: Pietra dura began under Jahangir at the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah at Agra, before the Taj Mahal.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Mughal architecture is correct?
o: The charbagh was introduced by Humayun
Shah Jahan's white-marble reign is called its 'Golden Age'
Akbar built mainly in white marble
Pietra dura was first used at the Taj Mahal
q.x: Akbar used red sandstone; pietra dura began under Jahangir and the charbagh under Babur.

q.s: The Anubhava Mantapa, the assembly of Virashaiva sharanas at Kalyana, was presided over by:
q.x: Basavanna set it up, but Allama Prabhu presided over it.

q.s: Basavanna served as treasurer at Kalyana under the Kalachuri king:
q.x: Basavanna, born at Bagewadi, served the Kalachuri king Bijjala.

q.s: The Srikalahasteeswara Satakam was written by:
q.x: Dhurjati, one of the Ashtadiggajas, wrote the Srikalahasteeswara Satakam.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (composer – work) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Venkatachala Mahatyamu is Tarigonda Vengamamba's; Kshetrayya wrote padams on Muvva Gopala.

q.s: The Telugu poetess Mohanangi was the daughter of:
q.x: Mohanangi, author of Marichi Parinayam, was Krishnadevaraya's daughter.

q.s: Madhura Vijayam, describing Kumara Kampana's conquest of Madurai, was written by:
q.x: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana, wrote Madhura Vijayam; Tirumalamba wrote Varadambika Parinayam.

q.s: Which of the following is regarded as a main reason for the defeat of the French by the British in India?
o: Absence of any base on the Coromandel coast
Refusal to take part in Indian politics
Lack of trading rights from the Mughals
Weak naval power and lack of steady home support
q.x: The French lacked naval supremacy and steady state support, while the English controlled the sea and had Bengal's revenue.

q.s: Who wrote of 1857 that 'what began as a fight for religion ended as a war of independence'?
q.x: S.N. Sen, author of Eighteen Fifty-Seven, gave this view; Savarkar called it the First War of Independence.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (historian – view of 1857) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Eric Stokes – Essentially a feudal rising
V.D. Savarkar – First War of Independence
S.N. Sen – Began as a fight for religion, ended as a war of independence
Rudrangshu Mukherjee – Peasant and taluqdar resistance in Awadh
q.x: Nehru called it essentially a feudal rising; Stokes saw many local peasant and elite risings.

q.s: Which battle is called the 'Plassey of Andhra'?
q.x: Chendurthi drove the French out of the Northern Circars and laid the base of English power there.

q.s: Robert Clive's defence of Arcot in 1751 took place during the:
q.x: Clive held Arcot for 53 days in 1751, in the Second Carnatic War, and then won at Arni and Kaveripak.

q.s: Dupleix became the Governor of Pondicherry in:
q.x: Dupleix was Governor from 1742 until his recall in 1754.

q.s: Satara (1848) was annexed by Dalhousie on the ground of:
q.x: Satara was the first state annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (territory – ground of annexation) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Awadh (1856) was annexed on the ground of misgovernance.

q.s: Which of the following treaties is NOT correctly matched with the Maratha party?
q.x: Rajpurghat (1805) was signed with Holkar.

q.s: The Treaty of Bassein (1802), accepting the subsidiary alliance, was signed by:
q.x: Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein, which led to the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

q.s: The All-India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at:
q.x: It was founded at Dacca at a session of the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference, on the initiative of Nawab Salimullah.

q.s: Who was the first president of the All-India Muslim League?
q.x: The Aga Khan was its first president; Ameer Ali set up the London Muslim League in 1908.

q.s: E.V. Ramasamy 'Periyar' launched the Self-Respect Movement in:
q.x: He left the Congress in 1925 and launched the Self-Respect Movement that year.

q.s: Periyar left the Congress in 1925 over caste segregation at the:
q.x: Separate dining for Brahmin students at the Cheranmadevi Gurukulam and the refusal of communal representation led him to quit.

q.s: Gandhi's principle of 'sarva dharma samabhava' means:
q.x: Sarva dharma samabhava is equal respect for all religions; welfare of all is sarvodaya and truth-force satyagraha.

q.s: Gandhi opposed all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Gandhi supported the remarriage of child widows.

q.s: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 at:
q.x: Blavatsky and Olcott founded it at New York; its Indian headquarters moved to Adyar in 1882.

q.s: Who was the first president of the British Indian Association (1851)?
q.x: Radhakanta Deb was president and Debendranath Tagore secretary.

q.s: Which of the following statements about pre-Congress associations of Bengal is correct?
o: The Bengal British India Society was formed with A.O. Hume
The British Indian Association was founded in 1836
The Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha (1836) was formed by associates of Rammohan Roy
Debendranath Tagore was the first president of the British Indian Association
q.x: The Bengal British India Society came with George Thompson, and Radhakanta Deb was the first president of the British Indian Association (1851).

q.s: Who presided over the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in 1891?
q.x: P. Anandacharlu presided at Nagpur (1891); Sayani presided in 1896 and Wacha in 1901.

q.s: Who presided over the Lahore session of the Congress in 1893?
q.x: Naoroji presided at Lahore in 1893, as he had at Calcutta in 1886.

q.s: Who was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons?
q.x: Naoroji won Central Finsbury in 1892; Lal Mohan Ghose had contested in 1885 but lost.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji served on the Welby Commission (1895)
Lal Mohan Ghose was the first Indian elected to the House of Commons
Naoroji won Central Finsbury as a Conservative
q.x: Naoroji won in 1892 as a Liberal and served on the Welby Commission; Ghose lost in 1885.

q.s: The boycott resolution of the Swadeshi Movement was passed at the Calcutta Town Hall on:
q.x: The boycott resolution was passed on 7 August 1905; 16 October 1905, the day partition took effect, was a day of mourning.

q.s: National Handloom Day, observed on 7 August, commemorates the launch of the:
q.x: Observed since 2015, it marks the Swadeshi Movement launched on 7 August 1905.

q.s: Who called Bal Gangadhar Tilak the 'Father of Indian Unrest'?
q.x: Chirol used the phrase in Indian Unrest (1910); Tilak sued him for libel. The title 'Lokmanya' came from the people.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the response to the Quit India Movement is correct?
o: The Unionist Party of Punjab actively supported it
The CPI supported it, calling the war an 'Imperialist War'
The Hindu Mahasabha actively supported it
The RSS kept away from the movement
q.x: The RSS kept away. The CPI opposed it, calling the war a 'People's War' after Germany attacked the USSR; the Mahasabha and the Unionists did not support it.

q.s: Which member of the Cabinet Mission (1946) was the Secretary of State for India?
q.x: Pethick-Lawrence led the Mission; Cripps was President of the Board of Trade and Alexander First Lord of the Admiralty.

q.s: The tomb of Alluri Sitarama Raju is at:
q.x: Alluri was shot at Koyyur in 1924 and buried at Krishnadevipeta.

q.s: Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj in 1909, aboard the Kildonan Castle, in which language?
q.x: He wrote it in Gujarati and translated it into English himself in 1910.

q.s: Hind Swaraj criticised all of the following EXCEPT:
q.x: Hind Swaraj attacked modern Western civilisation – railways, lawyers and doctors – and upheld village life.

q.s: The 'Drain Theory' was propounded by:
q.x: Naoroji set out the drain of wealth in Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.

q.s: Which of the following leaders was NOT an Extremist?
q.x: Gokhale was a Moderate; Lal-Bal-Pal were the Extremist trio.

q.s: The Borsad Satyagraha (1923) led by Vallabhbhai Patel was directed against:
q.x: It opposed a punitive tax, which was withdrawn.

q.s: Which of the following peasant struggles was NOT led by Vallabhbhai Patel?
q.x: Champaran (1917) was Gandhi's campaign in Bihar; Patel led Kheda (1918), Borsad (1923) and Bardoli (1928).

q.s: Vallabhbhai Patel was given the title 'Sardar' by:
q.x: The women of Bardoli gave him the title during the 1928 satyagraha.

q.s: Who is called the 'Patron Saint of Indian Civil Servants'?
q.x: Patel created and defended the All India Services and called the civil service the 'steel frame'.

q.s: In the April 1951 APCC election, N.G. Ranga was defeated by:
q.x: Sanjiva Reddy won by 5 votes; the defeat led Prakasam and Ranga to leave and form the KMPP.

q.s: Who was the chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission constituted in December 1953?
q.x: Fazl Ali, then Governor of Orissa, chaired it; S.K. Dhar headed the earlier Dhar Commission (1948).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953)?
q.x: The SRC had Fazl Ali, Kunzru and Panikkar; Dhar chaired the 1948 Linguistic Provinces Commission.

q.s: Who founded the Gorkha National Liberation Front (GNLF) in 1980 and coined the term 'Gorkhaland'?
q.x: Subhash Ghisingh founded the GNLF; Bimal Gurung later formed the Gorkha Janmukti Morcha.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 fixes the population ratio of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana at:
q.x: The ratio, based on the 2011 Census, is 58.32 : 41.68.

q.s: How many Schedules does the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 have?
q.x: It has 12 Parts, 108 Sections and 13 Schedules.

q.s: The prepared-core Levallois technique of making flakes is characteristic of the:
q.x: Levallois flakes mark the Middle Palaeolithic; blades and burins the Upper Palaeolithic.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Stone Age stage – tools) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Middle Palaeolithic is marked by Levallois flakes; microliths are Mesolithic.

q.s: The Brihatkatha was written by:
q.x: Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha in Paishachi Prakrit; Hala compiled the Gathasaptashati.

q.s: The Prakrit work Leelavati Parinayam is attributed to:
q.x: Kutuhala wrote Leelavati Parinayam, on Hala's marriage to Lilavati; Sharvavarman wrote the Katantra.

q.s: The Yashastilaka champu (c. 959 CE) was written in the Vemulavada Chalukya kingdom by:
q.x: Somadeva Suri wrote it at Gangadhara under the Vemulavada Chalukyas.

q.s: The Kathasaritsagara was written by:
q.x: It was written by Somadeva of Kashmir, a different author from Somadeva Suri.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Amaravati school of art is correct?
o: Its influence stayed within the Krishna valley
It reached its final phase under the Ikshvakus
q.x: The Amaravati school was indigenous, used white limestone, reached its final phase under the Ikshvakus and spread to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

q.s: The Satavahana king Hala married the Sri Lankan princess:
q.x: Hala's marriage to Lilavati is the theme of Leelavati Parinayam.

q.s: The Satavahana ruler Vasishthiputra Satakarni married the daughter of:
q.x: He married Rudradaman's daughter, as the Kanheri inscription records.

q.s: In which mudra does the Buddha's right hand touch the earth, calling it to witness against Mara?
q.x: Bhumisparsha is the earth-touching gesture; Varada is a lowered open palm and Abhaya a raised palm.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (mudra – meaning) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bhumisparsha – Calling the earth to witness
Dharmachakra – Turning the wheel of law
q.x: Varada is the boon-giving lowered palm; the Abhaya mudra is linked with subduing Nalagiri.

q.s: The first Sanskrit inscriptions of the Telugu lands were issued in the reign of the Ikshvaku king:
q.x: They date to Ehuvala Santamula, son of Virapurushadatta, who ruled about 24 years.

q.s: Sriparvataswami (Srisaila Mallikarjuna) was the family deity of the:
q.x: The Vishnukundins worshipped Sriparvataswami; the Salankayanas worshipped Chitraratha Swamy and the Kakatiyas Kakati.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (dynasty/community – deity) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Salankayanas worshipped Chitraratha Swamy (the Sun); Hariti was worshipped by the Ikshvakus.

q.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title 'Trisamudradhipati'?
q.x: Madhava Varma II was Trisamudradhipati; Govinda Varma was Shadabhigna and Vikramendra Varma I Mahakavi.

q.s: The Salankayana king Hastivarma of Vengi was defeated by:
q.x: The Allahabad Prashasti names Hastivarma of Vengi among the southern kings Samudragupta defeated.

q.s: Vengi was conquered from the Salankayanas by:
q.x: The Vishnukundin Madhava Varma II took Vengi from the Salankayanas.

q.s: The Chola king Rajadhiraja I was killed in 1054 in the battle of:
q.x: Rajadhiraja I fell at Koppam fighting Someshwara I of Kalyani.

q.s: Prataparudra Yasobhushanam, a Sanskrit work on poetics, was written by:
q.x: Vidyanatha wrote it; Ekamranatha wrote Prataparudra Charitra and Rudradeva the Nitisara.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Kakatiya-period author – work) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Rudradeva wrote the Nitisara; Prataparudra Charitra is Ekamranatha's.

q.s: Kakati Devi, the clan deity of the Kakatiyas, was originally the Jain goddess:
q.x: Kakatamma was originally Kushmandini; the early Garuda emblem also came from the Jain Tirthankara Shantinatha.

q.s: Rudrama Devi's daughter Mummadamma was the mother of:
q.x: Mummadamma married Mahadeva; their son Prataparudra II succeeded Rudrama Devi.

q.s: In the Kakatiya revenue system, 'Magani' land was:
q.x: Magani was wet land and Metta dry land; Dashabandhamu land for tank upkeep was tax-free.

q.s: Which of the following Kakatiya revenue terms is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Metta was rain-fed dry land; Magani was wet land.

q.s: The Bahmani Sultanate, the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan, was founded in 1347 by:
q.x: Hasan Gangu founded it at Gulbarga as Alauddin Bahman Shah.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Bahmani Sultanate is correct?
o: Alauddin Bahman Shah built the Gulbarga Jama Masjid
It was the first independent Muslim kingdom of the Deccan
Firuz Shah built an observatory near Bidar
q.x: Firuz Shah's observatory was near Daulatabad, the kingdom ended in 1527, and the Gulbarga mosque was built under Muhammad Shah I.

q.s: Who among the following supported the Kannada (Hoysala) theory of the origin of Harihara and Bukka?
q.x: P.B. Desai backed the Kannada theory; Sewell, Nilakanta Sastri and Venkataramanayya backed the Andhra (Kakatiya-service) theory.

q.s: The usual rate of land revenue in the Vijayanagara empire was:
q.x: It was usually 1/6, rising to 1/4 or 1/3 on fertile land; the land-tax documents were Adhuvanatantram.

q.s: Under his truce of 1364-65 with the Bahmanis, Kapaya Nayaka ceded:
q.x: He ceded Golconda, which became the boundary; Bhuvanagiri had been lost in 1356.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Ramappa temple is correct?
o: It was built by Recherla Rudra, a general of Ganapatideva
It is named after Lord Rama
It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019
q.x: Recherla Rudra built it; it is named after its sculptor Ramappa, was inscribed in 2021 and stands at Palampet in Mulugu district.

q.s: The Ramappa temple at Palampet was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
q.x: It was inscribed on 25 July 2021.

q.s: The mukha mandapam of the Srisailam temple is credited to the Vijayanagara ruler:
q.x: Harihara II added the mukha mandapam; Krishnadevaraya's gifts went mainly to Tirupati.

q.s: The Vizianagaram zamindari belonged to which family?
q.x: Vizianagaram was held by the Pusapati Rajus; Venkatagiri by the Velugotis, Peddapuram by the Vatsavayis and Bobbili by the Velama Ravus.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (zamindari – family) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Bobbili was held by the Velamas; Vizianagaram by the Pusapatis.

q.s: Veerapandya Kattabomman was the poligar of:
q.x: Kattabomman of Panchalankurichi was hanged in 1799; the Marudu brothers belonged to Sivaganga.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (leader – place) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Narasimha Appa Rao was the zamindar of Nuzvid.

q.s: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra to spread the Vandemataram message in:
q.x: Pal toured Andhra in April 1907; the Kotappakonda riots followed in 1909.

q.s: The Andhra Jateeya Kalasala at Machilipatnam was founded in:
q.x: It was founded in 1910 as a national school of the Swadeshi era.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 is correct?
o: It was shielded by the 7th Amendment (1956)
Tenants became direct ryots of the State
q.x: Tenants became ryots of the State; zamindars were compensated, and the Act was shielded by the 1st (1951) and 4th (1955) Amendments.

q.s: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao were kisan leaders of which district?
q.x: Both were Srikakulam kisan leaders; Gottipati Brahmaiah is linked with the zamindari ryot movement.

q.s: The publishing house 'Andhra Granthamala' was founded by:
q.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, founder of Andhra Patrika and Amrutanjan, also founded Andhra Granthamala.

q.s: The journalist Khasa Subba Rao founded the English weekly:
q.x: Khasa Subba Rao founded Swatantra and Swarajya; Andhra Patrika was Kasinathuni's and Krishna Patrika Mutnuri Krishna Rao's.

q.s: The Srikakulam tribal struggle (1968-70) was led by:
o: Tarimela Nagi Reddy and Chandra Pulla Reddy
q.x: Vempatapu Satyam and Adibhatla Kailasam led Srikakulam; Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal led Naxalbari.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (movement – leader) is NOT correctly matched?
o: People's War Group – Tarimela Nagi Reddy
q.x: The PWG was founded by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah; Nagi Reddy led the 1967 Andhra wing that split from the CPI(M).

q.s: The anti-arrack movement of 1991 began in Dubagunta village of which district?
q.x: Rural women of Dubagunta in Nellore, led by Rosamma, began it; arrack was banned from 1 October 1993.

q.s: The anti-arrack movement in Andhra Pradesh grew out of which adult-literacy programme?
q.x: It grew out of the Aksharajyothi adult-literacy classes in Nellore.

q.s: The actor Chiranjeevi received the Padma Vibhushan in:
q.x: He got the Padma Bhushan in 2006 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2024; the 2022 honour was Indian Film Personality of the Year at IFFI Goa.

q.s: As per NFHS-5, India's Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is:
q.x: India's TFR in NFHS-5 is 2.0, below replacement level; Andhra Pradesh's is 1.7.

q.s: Which State has the highest Total Fertility Rate as per NFHS-5?
q.x: Bihar has the highest TFR (about 3.0); per SRS 2024 Delhi has the lowest.

q.s: The Dayabhaga school of Hindu law is associated with:
q.x: Jimutavahana wrote the Dayabhaga; under it a son gets rights only on the father's death.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the schools of Hindu law is correct?
o: Vijnaneshwara lived at the Rashtrakuta court
The Dayabhaga was written by Vijnaneshwara
Under the Dayabhaga, a son gets a right by birth
Under the Mitakshara, a son gets a right to ancestral property by birth
q.x: Right by birth is the Mitakshara rule; Vijnaneshwara lived under Vikramaditya VI and Jimutavahana wrote the Dayabhaga.

q.s: Among the Ho tribe, 'Andi', the most esteemed form of marriage, is:
q.x: Andi is the traditional arranged marriage with bride price (gonong); Oportipi is capture, Raji-khushi elopement and Anader intrusion.

q.s: In the Manu Smriti, the 'Asura' form of marriage is one in which:
o: The daughter is given to a learned groom without dowry
The groom gives a cow and a bull
The daughter is given to an officiating priest
The groom pays a bride price
q.x: Asura, the purchase of the bride, is disapproved; Daiva is gift to a priest and Arsha involves a cow and a bull.

q.s: Which form of marriage in the Manu Smriti is regarded as the highest approved form?
q.x: In Brahma marriage the daughter is given to a learned, virtuous groom without dowry or bride price.

q.s: India's first, non-synchronous Census (1872) was held under the Viceroy:
q.x: It was held under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous Census came in 1881 under Ripon.

q.s: Which of the following statements about caste enumeration is correct?
o: The 1951 Census was the last full caste count
The 1872 Census was held under Lord Ripon
Since 1951 OBCs are enumerated by caste in the Census
The SECC 2011 was run outside the Census Act, 1948
q.x: The SECC was run by the Rural Development Ministry; 1872 was under Mayo, only SCs and STs are enumerated since 1951, and 1931 was the last full count.

q.s: Which feature of colonial rule led many caste associations to petition for a higher classification?
o: Ranking of castes in the Census
q.x: From 1871-72 the Census ranked castes, so caste associations petitioned to be placed higher.

q.s: The concept of 'Sanskritisation' was given by:
q.x: M.N. Srinivas coined Sanskritisation in his study of the Coorgs.

q.s: Sanskritisation of a caste usually brings about:
o: Structural change in the caste system
Positional change within the caste system
q.x: It changes a caste's position, not the structure; the claim succeeds only when others accept it, usually after economic or political gains.

q.s: Louis Wirth, in 'Urbanism as a Way of Life' (1938), explained urbanism by:
q.x: Wirth named size, density and heterogeneity; urban life has formal, impersonal ties and weak social control.

q.s: The 16th Finance Commission raised the share of urban local bodies in local body grants to:
q.x: It raised the urban share from 36% to 45%.

q.s: Shifting (slash-and-burn) cultivation in North-East India is called:
q.x: It is Jhum in the North-East; Podu is the term in Andhra Pradesh and Bewar in Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: Totemism among tribes, a clan's sacred bond with an animal or plant, goes with:
q.x: Members of a totemic clan may not marry within it: totemism goes with clan exogamy.

q.s: Untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form forbidden by Article:
q.x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; Article 15 prohibits discrimination.

q.s: Access to shops, public restaurants and places of public entertainment without discrimination is guaranteed by Article:
q.x: Article 15(2) guarantees access to shops and public places.

q.s: The Ranganath Misra Commission (1985) inquired into:
o: The demolition of the Babri Masjid
q.x: It probed the 1984 riots; Misra later headed the Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities (report 2007).

q.s: The Nanavati Commission on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots was appointed in 2000 by the:
q.x: The Centre appointed it in 2000 and it reported in 2005.

q.s: Under the POSH Act, 2013, the Local Committee for workplaces with fewer than 10 employees is constituted by the:
q.x: The District Officer constitutes the Local Committee.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the POSH Act, 2013 is correct?
o: Showing pornography is a form of sexual harassment under it
It applies only to government offices
One-third of Internal Committee members must be women
Its Local Committee is constituted by the State Women's Commission
q.x: Showing pornography is listed as harassment; the District Officer constitutes the Local Committee and half the IC must be women.

q.s: Section 326A of the IPC, added in 2013, deals with:
q.x: 326A is acid attack; 354B disrobing, 354C voyeurism and 354D stalking.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (IPC section added in 2013 – offence) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: 354D is stalking; sexual harassment is 354A.

q.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a 'heinous offence' is one carrying a minimum punishment of:
q.x: A heinous offence has a minimum of seven years; 16-18 year olds accused of one may be assessed for trial as adults.

q.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, the 'Children's Court' is a:
q.x: The Children's Court is a Sessions Court; the Board's preliminary assessment is not a finding of guilt.

q.s: The Union Ministry of Minority Affairs was carved out in:
q.x: It was created on 29 January 2006; Tribal Affairs was split off in 1999.

q.s: The Ministry of Welfare (1985) was renamed the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in:
q.x: The renaming came in 1998.

q.s: CLAP, launched in Andhra Pradesh on 2 October 2021, is a programme for:
q.x: CLAP (Clean Andhra Pradesh) is door-to-door collection of segregated waste.

q.s: The Jal Jeevan Mission, aiming at tap water for all rural households, is run by the Ministry of:
q.x: The Ministry of Jal Shakti runs the Jal Jeevan Mission.

q.s: Press Note 3 (2020) requires government approval for FDI from:
o: Countries with a trade surplus with India
Countries sharing a land border with India
q.x: It puts FDI from land-border countries, chiefly China, on the government route.

q.s: The 2020 bans on Chinese mobile apps were imposed under:
q.x: The app bans used Section 69A of the IT Act, 2000.

q.s: The US law that enabled civil nuclear cooperation with India, the Hyde Act, was passed in:
q.x: The Hyde Act (2006) came first, then the 123 Agreement and the NSG waiver in 2008.

q.s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group gave India a 'clean waiver' in:
q.x: The NSG waiver came in September 2008, after the 123 Agreement.

q.s: The WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine is being set up at:
q.x: WHO signed the agreement with the Ministry of AYUSH in March 2022 for the centre at Jamnagar, Gujarat.

q.s: The global Multidimensional Poverty Index is prepared by the UNDP with:
q.x: UNDP builds the global MPI with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative.

q.s: Which country became the 191st member of the IMF in October 2024?
q.x: Liechtenstein joined in October 2024, after Andorra (2020).

q.s: By IMF quota, India is the:
q.x: India is 8th, with about 2.75% of quotas.

q.s: IMF quotas determine all of the following EXCEPT a member's:
q.x: Quotas decide contributions, access to finance and votes; they do not fix exchange rates.

q.s: The Pravasi Bharatiya Samman is conferred by the:
q.x: It is conferred by the President; Satya Nadella was among the 2015 recipients.

q.s: The Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs was merged into the Ministry of External Affairs in:
q.x: Created in May 2004, it was merged into the MEA in January 2016.

q.s: The Supreme Court reviews its own judgments under Article:
q.x: Article 137 gives the power of review; Article 143 is the President's reference.

q.s: The advice given by the Supreme Court to the President under Article 143 is:
q.x: The advisory opinion under Article 143 is not binding.

q.s: Which Act allowed the legislative councils to discuss the budget and introduced indirect election?
q.x: The 1892 Act allowed budget discussion but no vote, and began indirect election.

q.s: The National Emblem in the original Constitution was sketched by:
q.x: Dinanath Bhargava sketched the emblem; Nandalal Bose led the Shantiniketan artists and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha illuminated the Preamble.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (artist – work on the original Constitution) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Prem Behari Narain Raizada – English calligraphy
Beohar Rammanohar Sinha – Illuminating the Preamble page
Nandalal Bose – Leading the Shantiniketan artists
q.x: Dinanath Bhargava sketched the National Emblem.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Indian Independence Act, 1947 is correct?
o: The Constituent Assembly also acted as the Dominion legislature
The British monarch ceased to be head of the Dominions
The Constituent Assembly was dissolved for fresh elections
The Governor-General acted on the advice of the British Cabinet
q.x: The Assembly was both constitution-maker and Dominion legislature; the Governor-General acted on Dominion ministers' advice and the monarch stayed nominal head.

q.s: The Interim Government headed by Jawaharlal Nehru took charge on:
q.x: It was announced on 24 August and took charge on 2 September 1946, with the Viceroy as President and Nehru as Vice-President.

q.s: The Muslim League joined the Interim Government in:
q.x: The League joined in October 1946.

q.s: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament is presided over by the:
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
q.x: The Speaker presides; the joint sitting is borrowed from Australia.

q.s: If a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflict, generally:
q.x: Under Article 254 the Union law prevails, unless a reserved State law has the President's assent.

q.s: The income limit for the OBC creamy layer, fixed in 2017, is:
q.x: The limit was raised to ₹8 lakh in 2017.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment allowed carried-forward reserved vacancies to be treated as an exception to the 50% ceiling?
q.x: The 81st Amendment (2000) inserted Article 16(4B) for carried-forward vacancies.

q.s: The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 gives effect to which Fundamental Duty?
q.x: 51A(g) covers the environment, wildlife and forests; the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act gives effect to 51A(a).

q.s: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of the:
q.x: The Swaran Singh Committee led to Article 51A in 1976; the Verma Committee (1999) listed laws giving effect to the duties.

q.s: The President prorogues the Houses of Parliament under Article:
q.x: Article 85(2)(a) is prorogation and 85(2)(b) dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

q.s: Supplementary grants are provided for under Article:
q.x: Article 115 covers supplementary grants; Article 116 votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants.

q.s: Votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants are provided for under Article:
q.x: These are in Article 116; an exceptional grant is not part of the current service of any year.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT vote in the election of the President of India?
o: Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
Elected members of the Delhi Assembly
Elected members of the Lok Sabha
q.x: Legislative Council members vote in neither the Presidential nor the Vice-Presidential election.

q.s: Who was the first Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy was the first; the post is not mentioned in the Constitution.

q.s: Article 164(1A) of the Constitution deals with:
o: The post of Deputy Chief Minister
The 15 per cent cap on the size of the Council of Ministers
The appointment of the Advocate General
q.x: Article 164(1A), added by the 91st Amendment, caps the Ministry at 15 per cent of the Assembly.

q.s: The 'curative petition' was evolved by the Supreme Court in:
o: Rupa Ashok Hurra v. Ashok Hurra (2002)
q.x: The curative petition was evolved in Rupa Ashok Hurra (2002).

q.s: Which of the following statements about contempt of court is correct?
o: The Constitution itself defines civil and criminal contempt
Only High Courts can punish for contempt
The 1971 Act followed the Sarkaria Commission
The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 defines civil and criminal contempt
q.x: The 1971 Act, based on the Sanyal Committee, defines contempt; the Supreme Court (Art. 129) and High Courts (Art. 215) can punish it.

q.s: Which of the following statements about judicial review in India is NOT correct?
o: It is a part of the basic structure
The Supreme Court exercises it through Article 32
High Courts exercise it through Article 226
The term 'judicial review' is expressly used in Article 13
q.x: The term is not used anywhere in the Constitution; Kesavananda Bharati and L. Chandra Kumar held it to be basic structure.

q.s: Marbury v. Madison (1803), the origin of judicial review, was decided under US Chief Justice:
q.x: It was decided under John Marshall.

q.s: The M.C. Mehta cases of the Supreme Court are usually cited as an example of:
q.x: The M.C. Mehta cases saw the Court issue policy directives; State of Rajasthan (1977) and Aravali Golf Club (2007) are cited for restraint.

q.s: Parliament may legislate on a State List subject in the national interest after a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article:
q.x: Article 249 needs a Rajya Sabha resolution; Article 250 applies during an Emergency, 252 on States' consent and 253 for treaties.

q.s: A law made by Parliament under Article 249 ceases to have effect after the resolution lapses, at the end of:
q.x: It ceases six months after the resolution lapses; the State keeps its own power meanwhile.

q.s: The CBI was set up in 1963 on the recommendation of the:
q.x: It was set up by a Home Ministry resolution on the Santhanam Committee's advice; it is not a statutory body.

q.s: The committee that selects the Director of the CBI does NOT include the:
o: Chief Justice of India or his nominee
q.x: The Director is chosen by the Prime Minister, the CJI (or nominee) and the Leader of the Opposition.

q.s: The Magna Carta was signed by King John of England in:
q.x: Magna Carta dates to 1215; the Glorious Revolution was in 1688.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (document – year) is NOT correctly matched?
o: French Declaration of the Rights of Man – 1799
q.x: The French Declaration of the Rights of Man came in 1789.

q.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is not legally binding because it is:
o: Only a draft of the ICCPR
A General Assembly resolution, not a treaty
Not signed by the permanent members
Not adopted by the Security Council
q.x: The UDHR (10 December 1948) is a declaration adopted by a General Assembly resolution, not a treaty.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Information Commissioner of India?
q.x: Wajahat Habibullah was the first CIC; Satyananda Mishra came later.

q.s: The Right to Information Act, 2005 came fully into force on:
q.x: It got assent on 15 June 2005 and came fully into force 120 days later, on 12 October 2005.

q.s: Justice N. Santosh Hegde's 2011 report as Karnataka Lokayukta exposed:
q.x: His report on illegal mining in Bellary led to the arrest of G. Janardhana Reddy.

q.s: The Lokayukta's jurisdiction extends to:
o: Legislative acts of the State Assembly
q.x: The Lokayukta looks only into administrative actions – corruption and maladministration.

q.s: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 under Article:
q.x: It was set up under Article 263; Article 262 deals with inter-State water disputes.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Inter-State Council is correct?
o: It was set up under Article 262
Its last meeting was held in 2006
It is chaired by the Union Home Minister
It is chaired by the Prime Minister
q.x: It was set up in 1990 under Article 263, is chaired by the PM, and its 11th meeting was in July 2016.

q.s: The Samajwadi Party was formed in:
q.x: The Samajwadi Party was formed in 1992; the Trinamool Congress was formed in 1998.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (party – year of formation) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Trinamool Congress was formed in 1998.

q.s: Which of the following regional parties arose as a split from a national party?
q.x: YSRCP, like the BJD, RJD and TMC, is a split from a national party; TDP, DMK and AGP are based on regional culture or ethnicity.

q.s: The mandal system, which ended the hereditary Patel-Patwari system in Andhra Pradesh, was introduced in 1985 by:
q.x: NTR's government introduced the mandal system in 1985.

q.s: The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR) is located at:
q.x: NIRDPR is at Rajendranagar, Hyderabad.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Panchayats under Part IX is NOT correct?
o: Chairpersons of the upper two tiers are elected indirectly
The minimum age for membership is 21 years
Members at all three levels are directly elected
The Constitution prescribes one method of electing the Sarpanch for all States
q.x: The manner of electing the village chairperson is left to State law; the other three are correct.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Gram Sabha?
q.x: 243A is the Gram Sabha; 243H taxes and funds, 243J audit and 243K the State Election Commission.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Article – subject) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: 243K is the State Election Commission; the State Finance Commission is 243I.

q.s: The People's Plan Campaign for decentralised planning was launched in 1996 by:
q.x: Kerala launched the People's Plan Campaign in 1996.

q.s: The holistic category of the National Panchayat Awards is the:
o: Nanaji Deshmukh Sarvottam Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar
Deen Dayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar
q.x: The Nanaji Deshmukh award is the overall category; the Deen Dayal Upadhyay award is theme-wise.

q.s: Which of the following States is fully exempt from Part IX (Panchayats) of the Constitution?
q.x: Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram are fully exempt under Article 243M.

q.s: In Arunachal Pradesh, which reservation under Part IX does not apply?
q.x: Arunachal has no SC population, so the SC reservation does not apply.

q.s: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha is provided under Article:
q.x: Article 330 covers the Lok Sabha and 332 the State Assemblies.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Article – content) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 332 – ST seats in State Assemblies
Article 330 – ST seats in the Lok Sabha
q.x: Article 15(4) allows special provisions for educational advancement.

q.s: Under PESA, 1996, ownership of minor forest produce is vested in the:
q.x: PESA gives the Gram Sabha ownership of minor forest produce.

q.s: Before land is acquired in a Scheduled Area, PESA requires that the Gram Sabha be:
q.x: PESA requires consultation, not consent; its recommendation is mandatory for minor-mineral leases.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the State Finance Commission is constituted every five years by the:
q.x: Under Article 243I the Governor constitutes the SFC; the 5th SFC was constituted in March 2023.

q.s: Which Andhra Pradesh committee on Panchayati Raj recommended direct election of the Sarpanch?
q.x: C. Narasimham proposed direct election on the Maharashtra model; Vengala Rao recommended no party symbols.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (AP committee – recommendation) is NOT correctly matched?
o: B.P.R. Vithal – Direct election of the Sarpanch
C. Narasimham – Direct election of the Sarpanch
Vengala Rao – No party symbols in panchayat polls
q.x: B.P.R. Vithal recommended Taluk Panchayat Samithis.

q.s: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 exempts strategic projects located within what distance of the international borders?
q.x: Strategic and security projects within 100 km of the international borders are exempt.

q.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, the cut-off date for occupation of forest land is:
q.x: Occupation before 13 December 2005 is recognised.

q.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, Other Traditional Forest Dwellers must show residence for:
q.x: Only OTFDs must show 75 years; forest-dwelling STs need not. Rights are heritable but not alienable.

q.s: PM-AJAY, a scheme for Scheduled Castes, is administered by the Ministry of:
q.x: PM-AJAY is run for SCs by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

q.s: The National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission aims to eliminate the disease by:
q.x: The target is 2047.

q.s: The District Planning Committee, which consolidates the plans of panchayats and municipalities, is provided under Article:
q.x: Article 243ZD, added by the 74th Amendment, provides for the DPC; 243ZE is the Metropolitan Planning Committee.

q.s: What share of the members of a District Planning Committee must be elected?
q.x: At least four-fifths are elected from among the elected members of the district panchayat and municipalities.

q.s: Which of the following was a stabilisation measure of the 1991 reforms?
q.x: Stabilisation measures were short-term (balance of payments, inflation, fiscal deficit) – devaluation was one; delicensing was structural adjustment.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the 1991 reforms is correct?
o: Stabilisation measures aimed at the balance of payments, inflation and fiscal deficit
Stabilisation measures were long-term, aimed at productivity
Industrial delicensing was a stabilisation measure
q.x: Stabilisation was short-term (devaluation was one such step); delicensing was structural adjustment.

q.s: How many members does the Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI have?
q.x: The MPC has 3 RBI members and 3 external members; the Governor has a casting vote.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's inflation-targeting framework is correct?
o: The MPC has four external members
It is based on the Bimal Jalan Committee
Price stability is its primary objective
The anchor CPI still has base year 2012
q.x: Price stability is primary; the MPC has three external members, the framework follows the Urjit Patel Committee and the CPI base is now 2024.

q.s: The NTPC Green Hydrogen Hub in Andhra Pradesh is being set up at:
q.x: It is at Pudimadaka in Anakapalli district, a JV of NTPC Green Energy and NREDCAP.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Phase I fishing harbour of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Juvvaladinne, Nizampatnam, Machilipatnam and Uppada are Phase I harbours; Pudimadaka is a Phase II site.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's grievance platform 'Meekosam' was launched statewide in:
q.x: Meekosam went statewide on 26 May 2015; it was followed by Spandana (2019) and then the AI-based PGRS.

q.s: The installed hydropower capacity of the Polavaram project is:
q.x: Polavaram has 960 MW capacity and diverts 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna.

q.s: The Veligonda project in Andhra Pradesh is named after:
q.x: Veligonda is the Poola Subbaiah Veligonda Project.

q.s: 'Water' is an entry (Entry 17) in which list of the Seventh Schedule?
q.x: Water is Entry 17 of the State List; inter-State rivers are Entry 56 of the Union List.

q.s: Which was the first State to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all buildings?
q.x: Tamil Nadu made it compulsory; Meghalaya was the first to approve a draft State Water Policy (2019).

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Monetisation Pipeline is correct?
o: Assets are sold outright to private firms
It is limited to the railway sector
The Government keeps ownership of the assets monetised
q.x: NMP leases brownfield public assets to private capital for a fixed period (PPP, InvITs, TOT), so ownership stays with the Government.

q.s: The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) was set up under an Act of:
q.x: NaBFID was set up under the NaBFID Act, 2021 with ₹20,000 crore paid-up capital; NIIF dates to 2015 and IIFCL to 2006.

q.s: In which stage of the demographic transition is Andhra Pradesh placed?
q.x: AP is in Stage 4 (low birth and death rates); its under-14 share is projected to fall to about 15% by 2036.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) covers:
q.x: PMSBY is accident insurance; death from any cause is covered by PMJJBY.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT covered under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana?
o: Permanent total disability due to accident
q.x: PMSBY covers only accidental death and disability; death from any cause is under PMJJBY.

q.s: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched on:
q.x: It was announced on 15 August 2019; under JJM 2.0 the deadline is December 2028.

q.s: Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, States other than Himalayan and North-Eastern States share the cost with the Centre in the ratio:
q.x: It is 50:50 for most States and 90:10 for Himalayan and NE States.

q.s: 'Naipunyam' in Andhra Pradesh is:
o: An AI portal for skilling and job matching
A household survey of youth skills
q.x: Naipunyam is the AI portal; the household survey is the Skill Census 2024.

q.s: Under the Super Six, 'Nirudyoga Bruthi' gives unemployed youth:
q.x: Nirudyoga Bruthi is ₹3,000 a month; Yuva Nestham was the 2014-19 allowance.

q.s: As per Census 2011, India's sex ratio was:
q.x: It was 940 females per 1,000 males, up from 933 in 2001.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Census 2011 is NOT correct?
o: India's population exceeded that of China
q.x: India's 121.09 crore was still below China's population.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Economic growth means qualitative improvement in capabilities
Economic development is measured by GDP growth alone
Economic development is narrower in scope than growth
Economic growth is a quantitative rise in actual output
q.x: Growth is quantitative (GDP, GNP); development is broader and qualitative.

q.s: In the Human Development Index, the maximum goalpost for expected years of schooling is:
q.x: Expected years of schooling has a maximum of 18 and mean years of schooling 15.

q.s: The goalposts for life expectancy at birth in the HDI are:
q.x: Life expectancy runs from 20 to 85 years; GNI per capita from $100 to $75,000 (PPP).

q.s: The World Bank (2013) estimated India's annual cost of environmental degradation at about:
q.x: It put the cost at about 5.7% of GDP (Rs 3.75 lakh crore, 2009), mainly via health costs and lost productivity.

q.s: The World Poverty Clock is run by:
q.x: The NGO World Data Lab runs it.

q.s: According to World Data Lab (2018), which country may have overtaken India as home to the most people in extreme poverty?
q.x: World Data Lab named Nigeria.

q.s: The World Bank's latest international poverty line, adopted in June 2025, is:
q.x: The $3.00 line uses 2021 PPPs; $2.15 (2022) used 2017 PPPs and $1.90 (2015) 2011 PPPs.

q.s: Unemployment arising from a mismatch between workers' skills and available jobs, needing reskilling, is:
q.x: Structural unemployment needs reskilling or reform.

q.s: Which type of unemployment exists even at full employment?
q.x: Frictional unemployment is short-term job-search unemployment present even at full employment.

q.s: The Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) was launched in which Five Year Plan?
q.x: IRDP came in the Sixth Plan; the Command Area Development programme was in the Fifth.

q.s: The Jawahar Rozgar Yojana was launched during the:
q.x: JRY began in 1989, in the Seventh Plan.

q.s: The phrase 'Hindu rate of growth' was coined by:
q.x: Raj Krishna coined it for India's slow growth of about 3.5%; the 1980s broke it, touching about 5.5%.

q.s: In the 1980s, under Rajiv Gandhi, industrial policy saw:
q.x: Licences were broad-banded and capital-goods imports eased; growth rose but was debt-fuelled.

q.s: GST subsumed all of the following taxes EXCEPT:
q.x: GST replaced many Central and State indirect taxes, ending cascading; basic customs duty remains outside it.

q.s: The Goods and Services Tax came into force on:
q.x: GST came into force on 1 July 2017.

q.s: The GST Council is provided for under Article:
q.x: 279A is the GST Council; 246A gives the power to levy GST and 269A covers IGST on inter-State supply.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Article – GST subject) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: GST is defined in Article 366(12A); Article 286 bars State taxes on supplies outside the State and on imports and exports.

q.s: The Economic Survey 2016-17 suggested that Central transfers to the States be linked to:
q.x: It found a suggestive negative link between transfers and States' own tax effort, so it argued transfers should reward effort.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a criterion for granting Special Category Status to a State?
q.x: The criteria included low population density, not high; high per-capita income was not a criterion either.

q.s: Special Category Status was granted to States by the:
q.x: The NDC granted it on the advice of the Planning Commission; the 14th Finance Commission made no distinction.

q.s: The 15th Finance Commission fixed the States' share in the divisible pool of Central taxes at:
q.x: The 15th FC gave 41% (42% under the 14th, 32% under the 13th).

q.s: Which new criterion did the 16th Finance Commission add for horizontal devolution?
q.x: It added 'Contribution to GDP' with 10% weight and ended revenue deficit grants.

q.s: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
q.x: The Prime Minister chairs NITI Aayog, which does not prepare Five Year Plans.

q.s: Zonal Councils, set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, are chaired by the:
q.x: The Union Home Minister chairs each Zonal Council.

q.s: Which State topped NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026?
q.x: Odisha topped the FHI 2026.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (NITI Aayog index – top State) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Tamil Nadu topped the Export Preparedness Index 2022.

q.s: To control inflation through open market operations, the RBI:
q.x: Selling G-secs absorbs liquidity; buying them injects liquidity and is expansionary.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a category of NBFC?
q.x: RRBs are banks set up under the RRB Act, 1976; CICs, IFCs and HFCs are NBFC categories.

q.s: The EASE (Enhanced Access and Service Excellence) reform agenda applies to:
q.x: EASE, launched in 2018, is for public sector banks and is run by the IBA's steering committee.

q.s: Deflation can set off a deflationary spiral mainly because consumers:
q.x: Postponed buying cuts profits and output, unemployment rises and the real debt burden grows.

q.s: During deflation, the real burden of debt:
q.x: Falling prices raise the real value of money owed.

q.s: The Union Government borrows on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India under Article:
q.x: Article 292 covers Union borrowing; Article 293 covers State borrowing.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's public debt is correct?
o: External debt makes up about 96.7% of public debt
Treasury bills form over 90% of Central debt
Debt is classed as internal or external by its maturity
Debt is classed as internal or external by the source of borrowing
q.x: The source decides the class; internal debt is about 96.7% and dated securities dominate.

q.s: As per the Union Budget Estimates 2026-27, the fiscal deficit is targeted at:
q.x: The fiscal deficit falls from 4.4% in 2025-26 to 4.3% in BE 2026-27; the primary deficit is 0.7%.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
q.x: Ministers' salaries are voted; charged items under Article 112(3) include the President's emoluments, judges' salaries and debt charges.

q.s: In fiscal policy, 'crowding in' refers to:
o: Rising tax revenue in a boom
Public capex drawing in private investment
q.x: Crowding in is public capex attracting private investment; India's capex multiplier is about 2.5-3.

q.s: A counter-cyclical fiscal stance means:
o: Deficits in slumps and consolidation in booms
Fixed spending regardless of the cycle
Surpluses in slumps and deficits in booms
q.x: Counter-cyclical policy spends more in downturns, as in Atma Nirbhar Bharat (2020), and consolidates in booms.

q.s: A tax whose rate rises as income rises is called:
q.x: A progressive tax rate rises with income, like income tax.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (type of tax – feature) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Proportional – One rate for all incomes
Progressive – Rate rises as income rises
Regressive – Higher share taken from low incomes
Degressive – One rate for all incomes
q.x: A degressive tax rises at first and then becomes flat.

q.s: Which of the following does NOT ordinarily help correct a balance of payments deficit?
o: Increasing government spending on domestic projects
q.x: Higher domestic spending raises incomes and import demand rather than exports.

q.s: In India's balance of payments, private remittances are recorded under:
q.x: Remittances are transfers (secondary income); interest, dividends and profits are primary income.

q.s: NRI deposits such as FCNR(B) are recorded in India's balance of payments under the:
q.x: NRI deposits are banking capital in the capital account.

q.s: The WTO Agreement on Agriculture came into effect in:
q.x: It came into effect with the WTO in 1995.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
q.x: The three pillars are market access, domestic support and export subsidies.

q.s: Under the Government of India's Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, prompt repayers get crop loans up to ₹3 lakh at:
q.x: Loans are at 7%, falling to an effective 4% with the prompt-repayment incentive.

q.s: Under the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme, the State pays the interest on crop loans repaid on time up to:
q.x: It covers loans up to ₹1 lakh; Pavala Vaddi, a State scheme, covered loans above ₹1 lakh up to ₹3 lakh.

q.s: The total credit potential estimated in NABARD's State Focus Paper 2026-27 for Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: It is ₹5.11 lakh crore, about 20% above ₹4.24 lakh crore; agriculture and allied is ₹2.55 lakh crore.

q.s: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane replaced the Statutory Minimum Price from:
q.x: FRP, linked to the sugar recovery rate, came in from 2009-10.

q.s: The State Advised Price (SAP) of sugarcane is announced by the:
q.x: SAP is fixed by State Governments; the FRP is fixed by the Centre on CACP's advice.

q.s: The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act was enacted in:
q.x: The order is IDRA 1951, MRTP 1969, FERA 1973 and SICA 1985.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (enactment – year) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: SICA was enacted in 1985.

q.s: India's first semiconductor wafer fab, by Tata Electronics with PSMC, is coming up at:
q.x: The fab is at Dholera; Tata's OSAT is at Jagiroad, Assam.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (semiconductor unit – location) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: India's first advanced 3D packaging unit is in Odisha.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's foodgrain production peaked at 123.57 lakh tonnes in:
q.x: The peak came in 2019-20; output had dipped to 108.39 lakh tonnes in the drought year 2018-19.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh contributes roughly what share of India's farm output?
q.x: AP gives about 10% of India's farm output.

q.s: In NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh scored:
q.x: AP scored 74 as a Front Runner; Kerala and Uttarakhand topped with 79 and India's score was 71.

q.s: Resettlement and rehabilitation of Polavaram project oustees is carried out under the:
q.x: R&R follows the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

q.s: The VB-G RAM G Act, which replaced MGNREGA, shares the cost between the Centre and the States in the ratio:
q.x: Under MGNREGA the Centre paid 100% of unskilled wages; the new Act shares it 60:40.

q.s: The 'Jeeva Kranthi' scheme of Andhra Pradesh provides:
q.x: Jeeva Kranthi gives sheep and goat units; Paala Velluva gives dairy units and Pasu Bhima Padhakam is livestock insurance.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (AP scheme – domain) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Jeeva Kranthi – Sheep and goat units
q.x: Paala Velluva gives dairy units to women.

q.s: In the regulated markets of Andhra Pradesh, the 1% market fee is levied on the:
q.x: The fee is paid by the purchaser and collected by the Agricultural Market Committees.

q.s: Since October 2015, Agricultural Market Committees in Andhra Pradesh pay what share of their income into the Central Market Fund?
q.x: They pay 25% of their income into the Central Market Fund.

q.s: The Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards were set up under the:
q.x: Both Boards were created by the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

q.s: Which allied sub-sector of Indian agriculture has grown the fastest since 2014-15?
q.x: Fisheries has grown at about 9.08% a year; livestock was about 30.87% of agricultural GVA in 2023-24.

q.s: Which mango varieties are identified with Andhra Pradesh's mango exports?
q.x: Banganapalli and Totapuri are AP's export varieties; Alphonso and Kesar belong to Maharashtra and Gujarat.

q.s: Free Trade Zones were set up in India mainly to:
q.x: Goods can be landed, processed and re-exported duty-free, making FTZs export platforms.

q.s: India's first Export Processing Zone was set up in 1965 at:
q.x: Kandla in Gujarat was Asia's first EPZ.

q.s: The Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor does NOT pass through:
q.x: AKIC covers Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, UP, Bihar, Jharkhand and West Bengal.

q.s: The Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor does NOT cover:
q.x: DMIC covers UP, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP and Maharashtra.

q.s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor programme is funded mainly by the:
q.x: ADB gives $625 million of $840 million (about 74.4%); the State gives the rest.

q.s: India's nuclear power reactors are operated by:
q.x: The Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd runs the reactors.

q.s: Within India's non-fossil installed power capacity, the largest share is from:
q.x: Solar leads; non-fossil sources made up over 54% of installed capacity by July 2026.

q.s: Which States topped NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2023-24 with a score of 79?
q.x: Kerala and Uttarakhand topped; Bihar was lowest with 57.

q.s: In the SDG India Index, a State scoring between 65 and 99 is classified as a:
q.x: 65-99 is Front Runner and 50-64 Performer; 100 is Achiever.

q.s: The mean distance of the Earth from the Sun is about:
q.x: Earth is 149.6 million km away; Mercury 57.9, Venus 108.2 and Mars 228 million km.

q.s: The White Rabbit timing protocol, used in India's GPS-independent IST network, was developed by:
q.x: CERN developed White Rabbit; the Jakkur (Bengaluru) network gives sub-nanosecond synchronisation.

q.s: The Tropic of Cancer and the Indian Standard Time meridian (82°30′ E) intersect in which State?
q.x: They meet in Koriya district of Chhattisgarh.

q.s: 'Bagan time', followed in the tea gardens of Assam, is:
q.x: It is an informal time one hour ahead of IST, not an official time zone.

q.s: Vega was the pole star about 14,000 years ago because of the:
q.x: The slow wobble (precession) of the axis shifts the pole star; Milankovitch cycles link such changes to climate.

q.s: Sea-floor spreading takes place along:
q.x: New crust forms at mid-ocean ridges; spreading can come in sudden episodic bursts.

q.s: An esker is a depositional landform made by:
q.x: An esker is a ridge left by glacial meltwater; yardangs and mushroom rocks are wind features.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a landform made by wind?
q.x: An esker is glacial; the other three are aeolian.

q.s: Uluru (Ayers Rock) in Australia is an example of a/an:
q.x: Uluru is an inselberg, an isolated residual hill.

q.s: A zeugen is a table-like ridge formed by wind erosion where:
o: A soft cap lies over hard rock
A hard cap lies over soft rock
q.x: A zeugen has a hard cap over soft rock; a yardang is a ridge parallel to the wind.

q.s: Iceland and the Azores rise above which submarine ridge?
q.x: Both stand on the S-shaped Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

q.s: The Ninety East Ridge lies in the:
q.x: It runs about 5,000 km along 90°E in the eastern Indian Ocean.

q.s: The Great Basin of the USA lies between the:
q.x: The Great Basin lies between the Rockies and the Sierra Nevada; the Great Plains lie east of the Rockies.

q.s: The West Siberian Plain lies between the Ural Mountains and the river:
q.x: It extends from the Urals to the Yenisei.

q.s: The Galapagos Islands belong to:
q.x: The volcanic Galapagos Islands are part of Ecuador.

q.s: The USA bought Alaska in 1867 from:
q.x: The USA bought Alaska from the Russian Empire in 1867.

q.s: Land and sea breezes are examples of:
q.x: They reverse daily, not seasonally, and moderate temperatures along the Andhra coast.

q.s: The minimum sustained wind speed for a storm to be called a hurricane or typhoon is:
q.x: The threshold is 74 mph (119 km/h); a super typhoon has winds of about 240 km/h.

q.s: Which of the following places does NOT have a Mediterranean climate?
q.x: Darwin in northern Australia has a tropical savanna climate; Perth, Santiago and Cape Town are Mediterranean.

q.s: In a positive Indian Ocean Dipole, the western Indian Ocean (Arabian Sea) is:
q.x: In a positive IOD the western pole is warmer and the eastern pole, south of Indonesia, cooler.

q.s: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol provides for the phase-down of:
q.x: Kigali phases down HFCs by 80-85%; the Montreal Protocol phased out about 100 ozone-depleting substances.

q.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: World Ozone Day is 16 September; 5 June is World Environment Day.

q.s: Which of the following statements about ocean currents is correct?
o: The trade winds drive the equatorial currents westwards
The Coriolis force deflects currents to the left in the Northern Hemisphere
The equatorial currents flow from west to east
Winds have no effect on ocean currents
q.x: Trade winds push equatorial currents west; the Coriolis force deflects to the right in the Northern Hemisphere.

q.s: The tide-raising force of the Moon, compared with that of the Sun, is about:
q.x: Being much nearer, the Moon's tide-raising force is about twice the Sun's.

q.s: Which Indian State shares international borders with China, Nepal and Bhutan?
q.x: Sikkim borders all three; West Bengal borders Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.

q.s: Which of the following States does NOT share a border with Bangladesh?
q.x: Nagaland borders only Myanmar.

q.s: The Papikondalu hill range lies along which river in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Papikondalu flank the Godavari gorge, with an average height of about 915 m.

q.s: Papikonda was declared a National Park in:
q.x: It became a wildlife sanctuary in 1978 and a National Park in 2008.

q.s: In the Koeppen classification, most of the peninsular plateau, including Andhra Pradesh, has the climate type:
q.x: The plateau is Aw; the Coromandel coast is As, west Rajasthan BWhw and Arunachal Dfc.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Koeppen type – region) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: West Rajasthan is BWhw (hot desert); Aw covers most of the peninsular plateau.

q.s: In Nepal, the river Gandak is known as the:
q.x: The Gandak is the Narayani in Nepal; the Saptakoshi is the Kosi.

q.s: The 'Sadanira' of the Shatapatha Brahmana is identified with the:
q.x: Sadanira is the Gandak; the India-Nepal Gandak agreement dates to 1959.

q.s: The Bhakra dam (Gobind Sagar) is on the river:
q.x: Bhakra is on the Sutlej; Pandoh is on the Beas.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (project – river) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Kishau is on the Tons in the Yamuna system.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (project – river) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Rihand is a tributary of the Son in Uttar Pradesh, not the Chenab.

q.s: The river Kaveri rises at Talakaveri in:
q.x: Talakaveri is in Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka.

q.s: The Mettur dam is on the river:
q.x: Mettur and the KRS (Kannambadi) dam are on the Kaveri.

q.s: The Raichur Doab lies between the rivers:
q.x: The Raichur Doab, long contested by Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis, lies between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra.

q.s: The Papagni is a tributary of the river:
q.x: The Papagni joins the Penna from the right near Kamalapuram.

q.s: The valley of the river Kundu in Rayalaseema is called:
q.x: The Kundu rises at Uppalapadu (Kurnool) and its valley is Renadu.

q.s: The Coringa mangroves are located in:
q.x: Coringa is in the Godavari delta near Kakinada; Bhitarkanika is in Odisha and Muthupet in Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (mangrove site – State) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Chorao Island, with the Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary, is in Goa.

q.s: The 2008 Bihar flood was caused mainly by:
o: A breach in the Kosi embankment
q.x: The Kosi broke its embankment at Kusaha in 2008.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (flood – main cause) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kerala 2018 – Heavy rain and dam releases
Mumbai 2005 – 944 mm of rain in 24 hours
q.x: The Chennai 2015 flood came from extreme rain and wetland destruction.

q.s: In disaster management, 'seismic retrofitting' means:
q.x: Retrofitting strengthens old buildings; restricting construction in flood areas is floodplain zoning.

q.s: Which of the following is a non-structural mitigation measure?
q.x: Awareness, early warning and land-use rules are non-structural; embankments and shelters are structural.

q.s: The High Powered Committee on Disaster Management, constituted in August 1999, was chaired by:
q.x: J.C. Pant chaired it; its report carried the theme 'Building a Culture of Prevention'.

q.s: How many types of disasters did the High Powered Committee (1999) identify?
q.x: It listed 31 disasters in five broad categories.

q.s: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 was enacted in the wake of the:
q.x: The Act followed the December 2004 tsunami and received assent on 23 December 2005.

q.s: The traditional water-harvesting system 'Khadin' is found in:
q.x: Khadins are earthen embankments across slopes in Jaisalmer; Eris are Tamil Nadu tanks.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (water system – State) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Eris are tank cascades of Tamil Nadu; kuhls are the diversion channels of Himachal Pradesh.

q.s: The Rashtriya Barh Ayog (National Flood Commission) was set up in:
q.x: It was set up in 1976 and reported in 1980.

q.s: The Rashtriya Barh Ayog put India's flood-prone area at about:
q.x: RBA's figure was about 40 Mha; the XII Plan Working Group (2011) put the maximum flood-affected area at 49.815 Mha.

q.s: Which country is the world's largest user of groundwater?
q.x: India uses more groundwater than any other country.

q.s: Groundwater over-exploitation in India is the most severe in:
q.x: Punjab is the worst, along with Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi.

q.s: Mangampet in YSR Kadapa district is famous for deposits of:
q.x: Mangampet has large barytes deposits; asbestos comes from Pulivendula.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (mineral – place in AP) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Apatite and vermiculite come from Kasipatnam.

q.s: Which source has the largest share of India's installed power capacity?
q.x: Thermal is the single largest, though non-fossil sources together exceed 50%; solar has overtaken wind among renewables.

q.s: Before the Green Revolution, India imported wheat from the USA under the:
q.x: Wheat came under PL-480; the Marshall Plan was for Europe.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Green Revolution is correct?
o: The HYV Programme began from Kharif 1966
India imported wheat under the Marshall Plan
The New Agricultural Strategy was adopted in the early 1950s
q.x: HYVP began in Kharif 1966 after the 1965-67 droughts; wheat came under PL-480.

q.s: India's cropping intensity in 2021-22 was about:
q.x: It was 155.4%; the net sown area was about 141 million hectares.

q.s: About what share of India's net sown area is irrigated?
q.x: About 56% is irrigated; drip and sprinkler cover only about 12% of it.

q.s: Muga silk, produced by Antheraea assamensis, is unique to:
q.x: Muga is found only in Assam; oak tasar comes mainly from Manipur.

q.s: Which State is the largest producer of mulberry silk in India?
q.x: Karnataka leads and AP is second; the Central Silk Board is at Bengaluru.

q.s: Small and marginal farmers (holding up to 2 hectares) form about what share of India's farmers?
q.x: They are about 86.2%; AP's average holding (2015-16) was 0.94 ha against 1.08 ha all-India.

q.s: In the Agriculture Census, 'semi-medium' holdings are those of:
q.x: Semi-medium is 2-4 ha and medium 4-10 ha.

q.s: The first integrated steel plant in India, TISCO at Jamshedpur, was set up in:
q.x: TISCO was set up in 1907; the order is Serampore paper (1812), Ranipet super-phosphate (1906), TISCO (1907), Bengaluru aircraft (1940).

q.s: India's first paper mill was set up in 1812 at:
q.x: The first paper mill came up at Serampore in Bengal.

q.s: India's first cement plant was set up in 1904 at:
q.x: The Madras plant used sea shells as lime; the first successful factory was at Porbandar (1914) by the Indian Cement Company.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a principal raw material of the cement industry?
q.x: Limestone, clay and gypsum are the main raw materials; bauxite is used for aluminium.

q.s: Which State is the leading producer of sponge iron in India?
q.x: Odisha leads and Chhattisgarh is second; India is the world's top sponge-iron producer.

q.s: Mini and secondary steel plants mainly use:
o: Scrap and sponge iron in electric furnaces
Iron ore and coke in blast furnaces
q.x: They melt scrap or sponge iron in electric arc and induction furnaces.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor is the first phase of the:
q.x: VCIC, India's first coastal corridor, is the first phase of the ECEC and is funded by the ADB.

q.s: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 between:
q.x: It ran 34 km from Bori Bunder to Thane.

q.s: Which is the largest single commodity carried by Indian Railways?
q.x: Coal leads; with 1,617 MT in 2024-25, Indian Railways is the world's second-largest freight railway.

q.s: Visakhapatnam harbour is shielded from waves and cyclones by the headland:
q.x: Dolphin's Nose (about 335 m) of the Yarada hills protects the land-locked harbour.

q.s: The Strait of Hormuz connects the:
o: Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman
Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden
q.x: Hormuz links the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (strait – waters it connects) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Turkish Straits – Red Sea and Mediterranean
Hormuz – Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
Bab-el-Mandeb – Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
q.x: The Turkish Straits link the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.

q.s: The KLI submarine optical fibre cable, inaugurated in January 2024, connects:
o: Chennai and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
q.x: KLI is Kochi-Lakshadweep; CANI connects Chennai with the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

q.s: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
q.x: Jantar Mantar was inscribed in 2010; Mahabodhi was 2002 and Mumbai's Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles 2018.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (World Heritage Site – year) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai – 2010
q.x: Mumbai's ensembles were inscribed in 2018.

q.s: According to the 1951 Census, India's literacy rate was:
q.x: It was 18.33% in 1951, rising to 34.45% in 1971 and 52.21% in 1991.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Census year – literacy rate) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Literacy was 64.83% in 2001; 74.04% was in 2011.

q.s: The Human Development Index does NOT include which of the following dimensions?
q.x: The HDI covers health, education and income; critics note it ignores sustainability and inequality.

q.s: Physiological density of population is the total population divided by the:
q.x: Physiological density uses arable area; agricultural density uses the agricultural population over cultivable area.

q.s: To be classified as a Census Town, a place must have a minimum population of:
q.x: A Census Town needs 5,000+ people, 400+ per sq km and 75%+ male non-farm workers; it is not a statutory town.

q.s: Many Census Towns in India are still governed by:
q.x: Census Towns are defined only by demographic criteria, so many remain under panchayats.

q.s: Which States recorded the fastest urban growth in 2001-11, largely due to reclassification of rural areas as census towns?
q.x: Kerala and Sikkim grew fastest because many villages were reclassified as census towns.

q.s: The Scheme for Protection and Preservation of Endangered Languages (SPPEL) is run through the:
o: Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysuru
q.x: SPPEL (2013) runs through CIIL Mysuru and covers languages with fewer than 10,000 speakers.

q.s: Bhasha Sangam (2018) was launched under the:
q.x: Bhasha Sangam is part of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat; the lack of a script is a major threat to tribal languages.

q.s: Khichan, a Ramsar site famous for demoiselle cranes, is in:
q.x: Khichan is in Rajasthan; Gogabeel is in Bihar.

q.s: Which of the following pairs (Ramsar site – State/UT) is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Patna Bird Sanctuary is at Etah in Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of sugarcane?
